public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Carbyon is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised €22.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a fragmented comp universe of nine private peers in Climate & Energy (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen) and one public comparable (LNZA), though none of these provide a sufficiently tight peer set for reliable same-stage or adjacent-stage median multiples.

The peer-median method is inapplicable here. Despite identifying nine same-sector peers, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints in any category—below the threshold for robust triangulation. An all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of climate and energy subsectors and their divergent capital intensity and commercialization timelines. The single public comp (LNZA) and the named private peers span wide stage and valuation ranges, limiting their direct comparability to a Series A round.

The absence of sufficient comps leaves traditional valuation methods constrained. Without a triangulated range, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation band. Key uncertainties include the subsector focus within climate and energy (which drives applicable multiples), the magnitude of any revenue or near-term milestones relative to peer stage, and the risk profile relative to the broader peer set. Additional disclosed financials or narrower subsector definition would be required to anchor a defensible range.
